title: Striped reclamation allocator with prefetch hysteresis and async eviction path
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Reduced tail latency for KV-heavy workloads by up to 28% in microbenchmarks; introduces a new striped reclamation allocator and async eviction/fallback path. No API or storage layout changes.
description:
Context and motivation: The paged KV cache has been a source of tail-latency spikes under mixed-read/write workloads. We observed eviction storms when hot ranges were repeatedly sampled by the global reclamation pass. This PR implements a striped reclamation allocator plus a prefetch-hysteresis heuristic and an async eviction slowpath to reduce stall amplification and improve locality.

What this changes (high level): Adds a striped reclaimer that divides the blockpool into lightweight stripes to spread concurrent reclamation work, implements an access-frequency-prefetch hint that primes adjacent pages on miss-heavy hot prefixes, and introduces a hysteresis threshold to avoid repeatedly prefeteching/evicting the same spans. Also moves expensive writeback scheduling off the fast path by introducing an asynchronous eviction queue processed by background workers; integrates with the scheduler to avoid eviction tasks blocking request threads.

Why this approach: Stripes reduce contention on a single global free-list and keep reclamation work proportional to active hot ranges. Prefetch hysteresis reduces oscillation between evicting and restoring the same pages when workloads oscillate at short timescales. The async eviction path prevents single-request latency from paying for I/O bound writebacks.

Compatibility and risk: No on-disk format changes. All behaviors are guarded behind a feature flag (env REDWOOD_KV_STRIPED_RECLAIM=1) and default to the existing allocator. We exercised both feature-flagged and default flows in CI and local perf runs.

Detailed changes (summary of commits): commit 1: bootstrap striped allocator scaffolding, add stripe metadata to block arena; commit 2: reclaimer algorithm and stripe-based free-list operations; commit 3: prefetch hinting and hysteresis policy driven by recent access counters; commit 4: async eviction queue + background worker integration with scheduler; commit 5: telemetry, unit tests, microbench harness and docs; commit 6: fix race in free-list handoff discovered during review.

Files touched (high level): pkg/kv/block_arena.go, pkg/kv/striped_reclaimer.go, pkg/kv/prefetch_hysteresis.go, pkg/serve/scheduler.go, pkg/kv/eviction_queue.go, pkg/metrics/kv_metrics.go, internal/bench/kv_hotspot_bench.go, docs/kv/allocator.md

Small illustrative snippet (striped free-list rotation):
- On allocation: map key hash -> stripe id -> try-local-free-list; fallback to global steal if empty.
- On reclaim: reclaimer picks stripes in round-robin and enqueues victims into async eviction queue instead of synchronous writeback.

Benchmarks and outcomes: Microbenchmark (kv_hotspot_bench) results on c5-like instance with 4 client threads: baseline median p99 latency: 720ms, after change p99 latency: 520ms (~28% reduction). Throughput under heavy mixed workload improved ~12% due to reduced stall time and localized reuse. Memory overhead: small stripe metadata (~0.7% of blockpool).

Tests: unit tests for allocator invariants, stress tests for concurrency and race detection, updated microbench harness. CI runs included a perf-job target that compares p95/p99 against baseline. One flaky test (pkg/kv TestEvictionOrdering) failed initially due to timing assumptions; it was made robust and re-run.

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Ramos: "Nice isolation of allocation fast-path; a couple of comments around the locking order in striped_reclaimer.go — can we instead use tryLock + backoff to avoid priority inversion?"
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed — I switched the stripe handoff to an optimistic try lock and fall back to a short backoff + yield. Updated comments and added benchmark showing no regression."
- Elaine Chung: "Prefetch hysteresis looks promising; request: make hysteresis threshold configurable via runtime knob and expose a metric for hysteresis-triggered-prefetches."
- Maya Patel: "Added REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_HYSTERESIS_MS env var and exported metric kv_prefetch_hysteresis_count. Also documented behavior in docs/kv/allocator.md."
- Samir Khatri: "Can we ensure the async eviction queue honors tenant priority?"
- Maya Patel: "Queue now reads a priority token from the request context; default behavior preserved for existing requests. Added unit tests for priority honoring."

CI summary and merge readiness: All required checks passed after fixes: unit, integration, lint, cross-compile. Perf job indicates consistent improvement and no regression on stable workloads. Security scan clean.

Merge outcome: Squash merge into main after approvals from Diego and Elaine. Changelog entry added to docs/releases/2025-11-21.md. Feature toggles documented for staged rollout.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-1301: evaluate stripe count auto-tuning based on active concurrency (linked linear).
- ENG-1357: extend telemetry to expose eviction latency breakdown per-stripe.

Notes for operators: Feature disabled by default. To safely roll out enable feature behind canary routing and monitor kv_prefetch_hysteresis_count and kv_eviction_async_queue_len. Watch for sustained increase in background writeback IOPS which could indicate too-aggressive eviction.
commits: bootstrap striped allocator and stripe metadata
implement striped reclaimer and free-list ops
merge_commit_message:
Striped reclamation allocator with prefetch hysteresis and async eviction (feature-flagged)

Improves tail latency for KV-heavy workloads by reducing eviction storms and keeping reclamation off the fast path. (ENG-1293, ENG-1301)
post_merge_actions: Add canary route, enable feature for 5% traffic, monitor kv_prefetch_hysteresis_count and kv_eviction_async_queue_len for 48 hours, then ramp to 25% and 100% if stable.
